name: Hathaway Clinic — the First Door
tagline: Clinic-shaped, not clinic-designed. Cassandra decorated it, and every woman meets the imagined version first.
body:
MOST WOMEN MEET HATHAWAY CLINIC ONCE IN THEIR IMAGINATION BEFORE THEY EVER CROSS ITS THRESHOLD. The imagined building has fluorescent panels, blank walls, stiff plastic chairs, and a reception window designed to make every private sentence audible from the far end of the room. Antiseptic, printer heat, old coffee. A clipboard before a hello. The wrong name called off a record, and then the injury treated as DATABASE WEATHER that no human being could possibly have prevented.

She rehearses the whole thing on the journey over. Why she has come. How firmly she will correct them. How she will leave if the room starts making her body sound like a problem.

THE ACTUAL FRONT DOOR OPENS WITH ONE SMALL BRASS CHIME.

Warm lamplight, honey floorboards, layered rugs, floral wallpaper, chairs in moss green and mulberry and faded rose and one astonishing mustard yellow that should be hideous and has somehow acquired authority. Crocheted throws. Mismatched ceramic vases of peonies, foxglove, lavender and sweet peas, cut that morning by a woman who decided they had a professional future. NOTHING MATCHES PERFECTLY. EVERYTHING BELONGS. Black tea, orange peel, furniture wax, warm biscuits, cut flowers. The clinical rooms beyond the parlour keep every standard Marianne demands of them; none of that sterility has been permitted to colonise the front door.

HATHAWAY CLINIC RECEIVES A WOMAN AS A GUEST BEFORE IT ASKS HER TO BECOME A PATIENT.

THE FURNITURE HAS OPINIONS. Deep without swallowing shorter legs, firm enough for a heavy body, generous through the hips. Armchairs leave room for broad thighs, a partner tucked beside her, or the fullness a woman may not have yet but has already begun imagining. Straight-backed chairs for anyone who hates being folded into softness; footstools for anyone whose feet would otherwise hover. NO PIECE OF FURNITURE ASSUMES THE WOMAN ARRIVING TODAY ALREADY HAS THE BODY SHE INTENDS TO CHOOSE.

CASSANDRA TESTED THE ROOM AGAINST THE BODIES IT WOULD ACTUALLY RECEIVE — recruited affirmed women and asked them to sit, sprawl, curl, cross, tuck, lean forward and complain with useful specificity. And BUILD mattered through all of it: a chest, waist, pelvis and pair of thighs do not become unrelated objects because different pages refine them. VALKYRIE'S load-bearing continuity, OPULENT'S pressure-sharing rest and ATHLETIC'S task-responsive recruitment could each reveal a different fault in the same cushion without anyone changing a measurement. A SEAT THAT SUPPORTED AN OUTLINE BUT PUNISHED THE WOMAN INHABITING IT DID NOT SURVIVE PROCUREMENT.

BELLA'S CONTRIBUTION WAS CHARACTERISTICALLY DIRECT. Forty-six-inch hips and a twenty-eight-inch waist were not an invitation to negotiate her down to a more convenient woman. The seat could accommodate her or Cassandra could find another seat. Bella remained entirely willing to make the rejected furniture's shortcomings memorable.

THE RECEPTION DESK IS A LOW CRESCENT OF OLD WOOD, NOT A BARRICADE. No glass. The receptionist looks up, smiles WITHOUT INSPECTING THE VISITOR'S BODY FOR AN EXPLANATION, and says the chosen name correctly on the first attempt.

THAT IS OFTEN THE MOMENT THE REHEARSED SPEECH DISAPPEARS. Some answer at once. Some laugh, because relief has chosen a strange exit. Some cry before they have taken their coat off. HATHAWAY STAFF DO NOT CONVERT ANY OF THOSE RESPONSES INTO A SYMPTOM. The tissue box is already in reach, plain and unceremonious.

THEN THE FIRST ORDINARY CHOICE IN THE BUILDING, WITH NO FORM UNDER IT: tea, coffee, water, or nothing yet. It is not a medical selection and it does not enter the Consent Menu. She may change her mind about the tea without discovering that somebody has made a FINDING about her readiness for affirmation.

Something foolish is always on the television at a considerate volume — today a reef shark whose hunting strategy consists of startling itself, losing the same fish repeatedly, and swimming into coral with growing personal resentment. NO SCREEN IN THE PARLOUR RUNS MEDICAL EXPLAINERS ON A LOOP. Nobody waiting to discuss her own affirmed body needs an animated diagram pursuing her across the room while she eats a biscuit.

THE ALCOVES ARE NOT BANISHMENT. Bookshelves, plants and thick curtains soften sightlines and noise while leaving the parlour one step away. She may talk, read, or hold a warm cup with both hands until her pulse stops trying to escape through her fingers.

THE LITTLE LIBRARY holds queer history, anatomy, genetics, poetry, battered fantasy, mysteries, romances, gardening books, memoirs, field guides and children's stories donated by the Hathaway daughters after they outgrew them. Pencilled notes from earlier readers. Tea stains. Corrections in Marianne's hand in the medical volumes. THE ROMANCE NOVELS MIGRATE ACCORDING TO THE STATE OF THE MARRIAGE — Marianne shelves them discreetly high; Cassandra returns them to eye level and adds recommendations. One thick novel currently carries two scraps of paper:

CASSANDRA, THIS DOES NOT BELONG BESIDE REPRODUCTIVE ENDOCRINOLOGY.
IT PRODUCED FOUR PREGNANCIES. THE SHELVING IS EVIDENCE-BASED.

THE PHOTOGRAPHS STAND AMONG THE BOOKS rather than gathering into a formal wall of achievement. Marianne asleep under a crooked birthday crown. Cassandra carrying three muddy daughters under her arms, grinning because gravity has again failed to impose consequences. A picnic that needs TWO FRAMES to hold all twelve girls, half of them looking at the camera and the rest committing smaller crimes against the food.

AND BESIDE IT, AN EMPTY FRAME. Marianne has written across the temporary insert: DAUGHTERS THIRTEEN THROUGH FIFTEEN ARE NOT AN ADMINISTRATIVE CERTAINTY. Cassandra has added YET beneath it in green ink.

CASSANDRA CROSSES THE PARLOUR with a vase of sweet peas — Junoesque, a cream dress scattered with tiny strawberries following the fullness of her chest and hips and the soft weight of her stomach, WITH POCKETS, because she considers pocketless clothing a patriarchal misdemeanour. Pruning shears in one. Wrapped caramels in the other, taken from the sideboard while believing herself unobserved.

COMMIT TO THE TURN, SWEETHEART. HESITATION RUINS THE ANGLE.
PLEASE DO NOT TEACH PREDATION IN THE WAITING ROOM.
I'M TEACHING CONFIDENCE.
YOU ARE COACHING A SHARK.
SHE CAME HERE FOR SUPPORT.

She gives the new arrival the same warm acknowledgment she gave the incompetent shark — ATTENTION WITHOUT APPRAISAL, WELCOME WITHOUT CAPTURE. She does not ask what body the woman wants. SHE DOES NOT ANNOUNCE HERSELF AS PROOF OF WHAT NEREID CAN DO. Her own body is allowed to be ordinary in the room it made possible.

MARIANNE FOLLOWS with one hand braced at the small of her back and a folder under the other arm, her dress loose over her middle. WHETHER THAT MEANS ANOTHER PREGNANCY, AN ACTUAL LUNCH, OR SIMPLY A COMFORTABLE DRESS REMAINS HER BUSINESS; the clinic does not turn a woman's abdomen into a public bulletin merely because its staff know how pregnancy works. NO WHITE COAT. A cardigan the blue of rainclouds, a pen leaked faintly near one cuff. She greets the visitor by her chosen name, introduces herself as MARIANNE, and asks whether she would like company for the first conversation — THE PARTNER ON THE SOFA DOES NOT RECEIVE AUTOMATIC ADMISSION, the woman who came alone is not treated as incomplete, and the answer may change whenever she wants it to.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE THIS. Cassandra remembered the rooms she was once expected to defend herself in. Furniture that made bodies into inconveniences. Questions asked before names. Cold light on skin. The habit institutions have of calling FEAR NONCOMPLIANCE. She could not rewrite anyone's journey to the clinic. SHE COULD DECIDE WHAT MET THEM AT ITS END.

So the parlour never asks a woman to prove she belongs there. No gratitude, no certainty, no femininity performed to clinic taste, no partner's endorsement, no tragic history, no sufficiently elegant explanation of the body she wants. THE DOOR STAYS VISIBLE. LEAVING REMAINS POSSIBLE. RETURNING REMAINS POSSIBLE. TEA CAN BE FINISHED WITHOUT SIGNING ANYTHING.
rules: Guest first, patient second. The parlour is not a waiting room
The chosen name, correct, on the first attempt
Tea, coffee, water or nothing yet — not a medical selection, not in the Consent Menu
No medical explainers on the television. Ever
Furniture procured against real affirmed bodies; a seat that supported an outline and punished the woman did not survive
A partner is admitted only if she says so, and she may change her mind
No white coat. She introduces herself as Marianne
